t73.bio: Ibn Hajar records Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Hawti, Abu 'Abdullah, as truthful, of the eleventh generation, who died in 79.

t7380.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Wasi' ibn Hibban al-Ansari al-Mazini al-Madani as a Companion, son of a Companion, though it is said he was rather trustworthy of the second generation.
as: It is said rather he is trustworthy, of the second generation.

t7555.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥayyān, Abū Ḥayyān al-Taymī al-Kūfī, as trustworthy and devout, of the sixth generation, who died in 45 AH.

t761.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṭāʾī al-Kūfī, known as al-Ḍakhm, as acceptable but accused of Shīʿī extremism, of the sixth generation.

t7641.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Dhuhlī al-Naysābūrī, nicknamed Ḥaykān, as trustworthy and a memorizer, of the eleventh generation, who died a martyr in the year 67.

t7797.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Yazīd Abū Murra, client of ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib (or of his sister Umm Hānī), as trustworthy, of the third generation, well known by his kunya.

t7902.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yūnus ibn al-Ḥārith al-Thaqafī al-Ṭāʾifī, resident of Kūfa, as weak, of the sixth generation.

t7977.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhrama as acceptable, of the seventh generation.

t8073.bio: Ibn Ḥajar reports Abū Khālid al-Wālibī al-Kūfī, whose name is Hurmuz, also called Haram; he is acceptable, of the second generation, came as a delegate to ʿUmar, and some say his report from him is mursal, placing him in the third.

t8187.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Ṭuʿma, a teacher of Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, said to be the Hilāl mentioned earlier; otherwise unknown, of the third generation.
as: Otherwise he is unknown, of the third generation.

t8204.bio: Ibn Ḥajar gives Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qalūrī al-ʿAṣfarī al-Baṣrī's name as Aḥmad or Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUbaydah, or ʿAbdak; he calls him trustworthy, of the eleventh generation, and says he died in the year 63.

t8415.bio: Ibn Ḥajar gives Abū Naʿāmah al-Saʿdī's name as ʿAbd Rabbihi, or ʿAmr, calls him reliable, and places him in the sixth generation.

t8590.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Rumaytha bint ʿAmr, a Companion who has a hadith on the death of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and another on the Ḍuḥā prayer, narrated from ʿĀʾisha.

t905.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records al-Jarrāḥ ibn Abī al-Jarrāḥ al-Ashjaʿī as a Companion who narrated few hadith.
